Rules: Adventure.text: ADVENTURE Making a hero, checks, rest and growth. ROUNDING When a rule divides a number, round the result up. S TAT S Each hero has 4 stats. Their class makes 2 of them Key Stats. STR Strength and toughness. A strong hero hits hard, carries a heavy load and endures many wounds. DEX INT CHECKS When the outcome of something is uncertain, the GM or the effect asks for a check, with a stat or a skill, such as a DEX check or a Stealth check. Roll 1d20 and add that stat, or the skill and its stat. If the total is higher than the DC, you succeed. A 1 on the die always fails, and a 20 always succeeds. When you fail, the GM chooses whether you fail or succeed at a cost. TA S K DC Agility and reflexes. An agile hero dodges blows, acts early in a fight and strikes with precision. Easy 8 Medium 12 Knowledge and reasoning. A clever hero understands magic, history and mechanisms, and solves problems. Challenging 15 Very difficult 18 Extreme 20+ Willpower, intuition and presence. A strong-willed WIL hero reads people, sways them and senses what others miss. A D VA N T A G E & D I S A D VA N T A G E KEY. When a rule says KEY, use one of your Key Stats. Stat dice. A stat written before a die is the number of dice you roll. With 2 WIL, WIL d8 means 2d8. In a favorable situation, the GM may give you Advantage. In a grim one, or for a long shot, you may have Disadvantage. SKILLS Both. Each Advantage cancels one Disadvantage before you roll. Each skill uses one stat. A check with a skill adds the stat and the skill. SIZE Arcana INT Knowing spells, magical items and magical creatures. SIZE ABOUT AS BIG AS S PAC E Tiny Fits in a pocket Several in 1 Examination INT Studying clues, wounds, traps and mechanisms closely. Small Fits in a backpack 2 in 1 Medium A human 1 Finesse Picking locks, disarming traps, sleight DEX of hand and steering a vehicle. Large A bear 2×2 Influence WIL Huge A small house 3×3 Insight Reading people and situations, WIL guessing motives and lies, having thought ahead. Lore INT Knowing history, kingdoms, religions and the creatures of legend. Might STR Lifting, breaking, climbing and swimming. Naturecraft WIL Surviving in the wild, finding your way, tracking and handling animals. Perception WIL Noticing what is hidden, who follows you and what is wrong. Stealth DEX Hiding, sneaking and slipping past guards unnoticed. Persuading, deceiving and performing to get what you want from people. Gargantuan A castle keep 4×4 or more HIT POINTS Your HP measure how much damage you can endure. Damage reduces them, but never below 0. At 0 HP, you are Dying, as the Combat page explains. Damage. Damage is any loss of HP. Damage stopped by Defend or by temporary HP doesn’t count as damage. Temporary HP. Temporary HP are lost before your HP. They don’t add up. When you would gain more, you choose which amount to keep. They are lost when combat ends. REST A Rest is a night of sleep, about 8 hours, somewhere calm enough to sleep. The GM says when the heroes can rest. Recovery. After a Rest, you recover all your HP, your mana, your class resources and the charges of your items, and you heal all your Wounds. Abilities limited per Rest can be used again. ITEMS You can carry 10 + STR slots of items, held, worn or in a pack. Each item card shows how many slots it takes (SLOT). Small related items share 1 slot, such as camping supplies. Ammunition isn’t counted. With a quiver, you have arrows. Level. You can use an item only if your level is at least the level shown on its card. Charges. An item may have charges (CHRG). Each use spends 1 charge, and they all come back after a Rest, unless its card says otherwise. MAKING A HERO 1. Class. Choose your class. Take its class sheet and the cards of its level 1 features. 2. Ancestry and background. Choose 1 ancestry and 1 background. Your ancestry gives your size and a trait. Your background gives another trait. 3. Stats and skills. Your stats and skills start at 0. Spend your 5 stat points and 10 skill points, as Leveling up explains. 4. The rest of your sheet. Fill in every other value of your hero sheet, as the Glossary page explains. LEVELING UP When the GM says your hero has earned a level, you gain it during your next Rest. Your class sheet says what you gain, in the row of your new level. Stat and skill points. Raising a stat or a skill by 1 costs as many points as its new value. Unspent points are kept. Advantage: Roll 1 additional die of the same type for each instance of advantage, then remove that many dice of your choice. Disadvantage: Roll 1 additional die of the same type for each instance of disadvantage, then remove that many of the highest results. When they tie, remove them from left to right. Dying: This creature can’t have more than 1 action per turn and can’t concentrate. Whenever it would take damage, it gains 1 Wound instead, or 2 on a critical hit.

Rules: Combat.text: C O M B AT Turns, actions, attacks, movement and adversaries. I N I T I AT I V E A N D T U R N S WEAPONS When the GM calls for Initiative, each hero rolls 1d20 and adds their DEX. The result gives the number of actions they have for their first turn. Each weapon card shows its damage, its Reach or Range, and its properties. I N I T I AT I V E ACTIONS 9 or less 1 10 to 19 2 20 or more, or a 20 on the die 3 Turn order. The heroes act first, in the order of the table, then the creatures. Hands. You have 2 hands. Each item card says how many hands it takes. Changing what you hold costs 1 action. Dropping an item costs none. Dual wielding. With a Light weapon in each hand, your first attack each round has Advantage. Unarmed strike. An attack with your fists or feet deals 1d4+STR damage, with Reach 1. REACH, RANGE AND AREAS Limits. Limits per turn and per round reset at the end of your turn. An ability limited per turn can be used again on another creature’s turn. Each attack or ability says how far it reaches, or the shape of its area. ACTIONS Reach X. A melee attack reaches every space within X spaces. Without a number, it is Reach 1. At the end of your turn, you lose the actions you have left and get 3 new ones. You spend them on your turn, or when a triggered action allows it. Range X. A ranged attack reaches X spaces, or up to twice that with Disadvantage. It has Disadvantage while an enemy is adjacent to you. Which actions. Every hero can take the actions of the Basic Actions, Grapple and Triggered Actions cards, and of their class and spell cards. Cone X. It starts at you and goes X spaces out, and X spaces wide at its far end. Triggered actions. An action that starts with “When…” is used when its trigger happens, even outside your turn. You may decide after seeing the roll. Line X. It goes X spaces in a straight line from you, 1 space wide. Areas. A space at least half covered by an area is part of it. Over several turns. An ability that costs more actions than you have can be paid over several turns. You must keep your Concentration, and do nothing else that costs an action in the meantime. Obstacles between you and a ranged attacker give you Cover or Full Cover, and let you Hide. MOVEMENT Hiding. Most creatures won’t hunt a hidden hero while other dangers remain. Your speed is 6. Your cards may change it. Other creatures. You may move through an ally’s space. You may move through an enemy’s space only if its size is at least 2 steps bigger or smaller than yours. You can’t end your move in an occupied space. AT TAC K Any spell or ability that can harm an enemy is an attack. Roll its dice and deal that much damage. Its Primary Die can miss or crit. Areas. An attack on an area can’t miss and can’t crit. Roll its damage once and apply it to every creature in the area. If it calls for a check, each creature rolls its own. A condition that gives Advantage or Disadvantage against one creature, such as Prone, doesn’t change the roll. Rushed attacks. Each attack after the first on the same turn has 1 more Disadvantage. Defense. A creature takes its Defense less damage from each attack. A hero’s Defense only counts when they Defend. Critical hits ignore Defense. Vulnerable and Resistant. A creature takes 10 more damage from a type it is Vulnerable to, and 10 less damage from a type it is Resistant to. COVER AND HIDING DYING AND WOUNDS Wounds are lasting injuries. You die when you have 6 Wounds. A Rest heals all of them. Gaining Wounds. When you drop to 0 HP, you gain 1 Wound and you are Dying until you regain HP. While Dying, each time you would take damage, you gain 1 Wound instead, or 2 on a critical hit. Some cards also make you gain Wounds. ARMOR AND SHIELDS Your Defense is your DEX, plus the bonus of your armor and of your shield. Their bonus grows with your level, as their cards show. Proficiency. You can wear only the armor, and hold only the shields, your class sheet lists. ADVERSARIES Adversaries are the creatures the GM plays. Each has 1 action per turn, or the number its card shows as ACT. It moves up to its speed for free, without spending an action. Only heroes make opportunity attacks. Stats and skills. An adversary’s STR, DEX, INT, WIL and skills are 0, unless its card shows them. Minions. Any damage kills this creature. Its attacks can’t crit and ignore Advantage and Disadvantage. When several minions attack the same creature, their damage counts as a single attack. Building an encounter. Add up the heroes’ levels, then the adversaries’ levels. When the two totals are equal, the fight is balanced. Fewer adversary levels make it easier, more make it harder. Advantage: Roll 1 additional die of the same type for each instance of advantage, then remove that many dice of your choice. Concentration: You can concentrate on only 1 spell or ability at a time. When you take a critical hit while concentrating, your concentration ends. You can’t concentrate while Dying or Incapacitated. Cover: An obstacle partially blocks a creature’s line of attack to you, so its ranged attacks against you have disadvantage. Disadvantage: Roll 1 additional die of the same type for each instance of disadvantage, then remove that many of the highest results. When they tie, remove them from left to right. Dying: This creature can’t have more than 1 action per turn and can’t concentrate. Whenever it would take damage, it gains 1 Wound instead, or 2 on a critical hit. Full Cover: An obstacle completely blocks a creature’s line of attack to you, so it cannot target you with ranged attacks. Hide: Spend 1 action to Hide from the creatures you have Cover from. Your next attack has advantage, then you lose Hide. Primary Die: The leftmost die of an attack’s damage. On a 1, the attack misses and has no effect. On its maximum, the attack is a critical hit: roll that die again and add the result, as long as you roll the maximum. Prone: This creature’s movement costs twice as much. Its attacks have disadvantage. Melee attacks against it have advantage. Ranged attacks against it have disadvantage. It may spend 3 spaces of movement to stand up.

Rules: Glossary.text: GLOSSARY Every condition, keyword and abbreviation, and how to fill in your hero sheet. CONDITIONS A creature has a condition or doesn’t. Conditions don’t stack. Asleep: This creature is Incapacitated until two of its turns have passed or until it takes damage. Blind: This creature can’t see. Attacks against it have advantage. Its attacks have disadvantage. Bloodied: This creature is at half its max HP or less. Charged: This condition has no effect on its own. Any effect that relies on it ends it. It ends when combat ends. A creature that takes lightning damage becomes Charged. Charmed: This creature treats the charmer as an ally. The charmer has advantage on social interactions with it. Dazed: If this creature is a hero, it loses 1 action. If it is a monster, it has 1 fewer action on its next turn. Dying: This creature can’t have more than 1 action per turn and can’t concentrate. Whenever it would take damage, it gains 1 Wound instead, or 2 on a critical hit. Empowered X: This creature’s attacks deal X more damage. Frightened: This creature has disadvantage on rolls while the source of its fear is nearby. Its speed is halved while it moves closer to that source. Grappled: This creature can’t move. Attacks against it have advantage. The grapple ends when the creature grappling it lets go, moves away, or is Incapacitated. Hampered: This creature’s actions or movement are reduced, for example by Dazed, Grappled, Prone, or Difficult Terrain. Incapacitated: This creature can’t do anything. Attacks against it have advantage. Melee attacks that hit it are critical hits. Invisible: This creature can’t be seen. Its attacks have advantage. Attacks against it have disadvantage. Petrified: This creature is Incapacitated. It is immune to most damage, except from large explosions, picks, or similar tools. Poisoned: This creature has disadvantage on rolls. Prone: This creature’s movement costs twice as much. Its attacks have disadvantage. Melee attacks against it have advantage. Ranged attacks against it have disadvantage. It may spend 3 spaces of movement to stand up. Restrained: This creature can’t move. Attacks against it have advantage. Riding: This creature moves with its mount. Attacks that miss it hit its mount instead. Silenced: This creature can’t cast spells or use abilities that require speaking. Slowed: This creature’s speed is halved during its next turn. Smoldering: This condition has no effect on its own. Any effect that relies on it ends it. It ends when combat ends. Taunted: This creature has disadvantage on attacks, except against its most recent taunter. Weakened X: This creature’s attacks deal X less damage. Wounded: This creature has at least 1 Wound. A hero typically dies at 6 Wounds. KEYWORDS Keywords are the words every card uses the same way. Each card reminds the ones it uses. GENERAL Advantage: Roll 1 additional die of the same type for each instance of advantage, then remove that many dice of your choice. Aura: Every space within its Reach of you, yours included. It moves with you. Blindsight X: This creature can sense creatures and obstacles within X spaces, ignoring Blind, darkness, and invisibility. Concentration: You can concentrate on only 1 spell or ability at a time. When you take a critical hit while concentrating, your concentration ends. You can’t concentrate while Dying or Incapacitated. Cover: An obstacle partially blocks a creature’s line of attack to you, so its ranged attacks against you have disadvantage. D44: Roll 2d4. The leftmost die is the tens digit, and the other die is the ones digit. D66: Roll 2d6. The leftmost die is the tens digit, and the other die is the ones digit. D88: Roll 2d8. The leftmost die is the tens digit, and the other die is the ones digit. Difficult Terrain: Each space of Difficult Terrain costs 2 spaces of movement. Disadvantage: Roll 1 additional die of the same type for each instance of disadvantage, then remove that many of the highest results. When they tie, remove them from left to right. Distracted: A creature is Distracted if it is adjacent to or Taunted by one of your allies, if it can’t see you, or if you have Hide from it. Flying: This creature can move through the air at its normal speed. Knockback pushes it twice as far. Full Cover: An obstacle completely blocks a creature’s line of attack to you, so it cannot target you with ranged attacks. Hide: Spend 1 action to Hide from the creatures you have Cover from. Your next attack has advantage, then you lose Hide. Interpose: When a creature within 2 spaces of you would be hit by an attack, you may spend 1 action to become the new target of that attack. You move into its space, and it moves to an adjacent space of its choice. You can do this once per round. Knockback X: Push this creature X spaces away. If an obstacle stops it, it and the creature it hits each take damage equal to the pusher’s LVL+1 per space it didn’t move. Small, Tiny and Flying creatures are pushed twice as far, Large ones half as far, and Huge and Gargantuan ones not at all. Primary Die: The leftmost die of an attack’s damage. On a 1, the attack misses and has no effect. On its maximum, the attack is a critical hit: roll that die again and add the result, as long as you roll the maximum. Swarm: This creature can move into and stay in the space of other creatures. It can attack the creatures in its space. Vulnerable: This creature takes 10 additional damage from the listed damage type. CLASS Some classes have keywords of their own. Demand Control: Choose 1 option from the Control Table that you haven’t chosen yet. All options become available again when you roll Initiative or once you have chosen each of them. Direbeast Form: Fearsome Beast, Beast of the Pack or Beast of Nightmares, taken with Beastshift. Invoke Chaos: Roll a d20 on the Chaos Table (Magic page). Marked: A creature is Marked when you target it with Hunter's Mark. It is Marked only for you. Raging: You are Raging until you leave combat, you drop to 0 HP, or you go 1 round without attacking or using Rage. EQUIPMENT A B B R E V I AT I O N S The short words used by the rules. STR Strength, one of your 4 stats. DEX Dexterity, one of your 4 stats. INT Intelligence, one of your 4 stats. WIL Willpower, one of your 4 stats. KEY One of your Key Stats, the 2 stats your class sheet names. LVL Your level. HP Hit points. DC The number a check must beat to succeed. GM The Game Master. What you carry, and the room you have for it. VA L U E HOW TO FILL IT IN Slots used Sum of SLOT, out of 10 + STR Add up the SLOT of every item you carry. Your maximum is 10 plus your STR. Magic items 2, + 1 at levels 5, 10 and 15 The magic items you carry, out of the number your class sheet gives for your level. Armor, Shield The armor and the shield you wear, if any. Items SLOT of each item Each item you carry, with its SLOT. C O M B AT HERO SHEET Each value of your hero sheet, with its formula and how to fill it in. Write in pencil, since most values change as you level up. The values you use in a fight. VA L U E HOW TO FILL IT IN Max HP 10 + LVL×Vitality Raise it each time you gain a level or your Vitality changes. Current HP Max HP − damage Take off the damage you take, and add what you heal, up to your max. A Rest brings it back to your max. Temp HP The temporary HP an effect gives you. They are lost when combat ends. Defense DEX + armor DEF + shield DEF Your DEX, plus the DEF of the armor and of the shield you wear. Initiative DEX What you add to your Initiative roll. Speed 6 How many spaces you move. Some cards change it. Mana Your mana pool card Its max is on your class’s mana pool card. Spend it on tiered spells. A Rest brings it back. Resource Its card The name and the max of a class resource, such as Fury Dice, from its card. Wounds 6 at most Tick 1 circle for each Wound. At the 6th, you die. A Rest clears them all. Some ancestries change the number. IDENTITY VA L U E HOW TO FILL IT IN Hero, Player Your hero’s name and yours. Class, Subclass Your class sheet. You choose your subclass when your class sheet says so. Ancestry, Background The cards you chose. Level 1 + levels gained 1 at first, then 1 more each time the GM gives you a level. Vitality Class Vitality + STR The Vitality of your class sheet, plus your STR. Size Ancestry size The size your ancestry card gives. N A R R AT I V E Your stats, your skills and the points you have left to spend. VA L U E HOW TO FILL IT IN Stat points 5 + (LVL − 1) − spent 5 at level 1 and 1 more at each level. Take off the points you spend. Unspent points are kept. Skill points 10 + 2×(LVL − 1) − spent 10 at level 1 and 2 more at each level. Take off the points you spend. KEY Tick the 2 Key Stats your class sheet names. Stat Raising it to N costs N 0 at first. Raising a stat by 1 costs as many stat points as its new value, so going from 2 to 3 costs 3. Skill Raising it to N costs N 0 at first. Raising a skill by 1 costs as many skill points as its new value. Total Stat + Skill What you add to a check with that skill. LEVELS VA L U E HOW TO FILL IT IN Levels At each level, what you gained and what you chose, from the row of that level on your class sheet. CAPSULES CARDS The letters below the name of each kind of card, then the capsules above their effects. SPELLS The dark capsule says what kind of effect follows. The outlined capsules after it give its cost, its limits and its attack. Narrative An effect for exploration and role-play, such as Advantage on some checks. ACT The actions it costs. With no ACT, its text says how it is cast. Passive Always on, or triggered on its own. It costs no action. MANA The mana it costs, equal to its tier. Cantrips cost none. Active You choose to use it, and pay what the outlined capsules show. CAST Its casting time, in minutes, for a spell cast outside combat. Lost What a subclass takes away from your class. CONC It needs Concentration, for up to this long. Levels What changes as you level up. Each line gives the value from that level on, and replaces the one before. Upcast What each extra mana adds to the spell. X Actions The actions it costs. X Mana The mana it costs. X Charges The charges of the item it spends. A class resource works the same way, such as X TotH charges . X Wounds You gain that many Wounds to use it. X/Turn How many times you can use it per turn. X/ Round, X/Encounter and X/Rest work the same way. KEY/Rest As many times as your KEY between two Rest periods. DMG The damage it deals. RNGE How far away its target can be. REACH How far around you it reaches, or the shape of its area, such as Cone 4. AREA The size of the area it affects. ITEMS Weapons, armor and other items. LVL The level you need to use it. DMG The damage of a weapon. DEF The Defense bonus of an armor or a shield. REACH How far a melee weapon reaches. RNGE How far a ranged weapon reaches. CHRG Its charges. Each use spends 1, and they come back after a Rest. AoE It affects an area, and the Areas rule of the Combat page applies. SLOT The inventory slots it takes. X Attacks The number of attacks it makes. Reach X How far its attack reaches. A Range capsule works the same way. XdY Damage The damage of its attack. C R E AT U R E S ACT Its actions per turn. With no ACT, it has 1. HP Its hit points. DEF Its Defense, taken off the damage of each attack. SPD Its speed. With no SPD, it is 6. SIZ Its size, T for Tiny, S for Small, L for Large, H for Huge and G for Gargantuan. With no SIZ, it is Medium. LVL Its level, for Building an encounter. STR Its Strength. With no STR, it is 0. DEX Its Dexterity. With no DEX, it is 0. INT Its Intelligence. With no INT, it is 0. WIL Its Willpower. With no WIL, it is 0. CLASSES Some class resources have a short name. TotH Thrill of the Hunt charges, for the Hunter. Mom Momentum charges, for the Zephyr. BoS Burst of Speed charges, for the Zephyr.

Rules: Magic.text: MAGIC Spells, mana, upcasting and chaos. SPELLS READING A SPELL CARD There are 6 schools of magic. Each school has cantrips and 9 tiers of spells. You can cast any spell of a school you know, up to the highest tier you have unlocked. Your class sheet says which schools and tiers you get, and you hold a card for each of your spells. The letters at the top of a spell card, such as ACT, MANA or RNGE, are explained on the Glossary page. Damage type. A spell deals damage of its school’s type, unless it says otherwise. Some classes also learn utility spells. They are tools for exploration and daily life, rather than for fighting. Many take minutes to cast, as their CAST shows, and are cast outside combat. SCHOOL STRENGTHS Fire High, steady damage at medium range. Some spells make creatures Smoldering and do more against them. Ice Medium damage at long range, control of the battlefield, protection of the caster. Some spells do more against Hampered creatures. Lightning High damage at long range, teleportation, metal targets. Some spells can hurt the caster. Necrotic Minions, traps and control. Some spells prey on Bloodied creatures, allies included. Radiant Strong against the undead and the frightened. Protection, healing, and even a return to life. Wind Moving friends and foes, cutting through groups. Some spells deal more damage on a critical hit. CASTING A SPELL Casting a spell costs the actions its card shows. You need a free hand, and you must be able to speak. A Silenced creature can’t cast spells. Range and reach. A spell with a range has Disadvantage while an enemy is adjacent to you, like any ranged attack. A spell with a reach doesn’t. Several targets. A spell that targets several creatures rolls its attack for each one, like separate attacks. Defensive spells. A spell you may cast while Defending costs no action. You can cast it only while you Defend. MANA Tiered spells cost mana. A spell’s mana cost equals its tier. Cantrips cost no mana. Mana pool. Your class card says how much mana you have and how you recover it, such as the Mage Mana Pool, Oathsworn Mana Pool or Shepherd Mana Pool. UPCASTING When you cast a tiered spell, you may spend more mana than its tier, up to the highest tier you have unlocked. For each extra mana, the spell gains its Upcast effect once. Several Upcast effects. When a spell has several Upcast effects, choose one of them for each extra mana. CANTRIPS Cantrips grow stronger as you level up. Their Levels section says how, and at which levels. UTILITY SPELLS CHAOS TABLE When an effect tells you to Invoke Chaos, roll a d20 on this table.
